description: Manage application lifecycle: list all running user-facing apps, get the frontmost app, launch or activate an app, gracefully quit or force-quit a process, or hide/show an app. Launch activates the app if already running; use hidden=true to start in the background without bringing it forward. Force-quit terminates immediately (SIGKILL) without saving. Hide and show require Accessibility permission.

action.description: Operation to perform on the application.

app_name.description: Application name, e.g. "Safari", "Visual Studio Code". Used by launch (or bundle_id), quit, force_quit, hide, and show.

bundle_id.description: Bundle identifier, e.g. "com.apple.Safari". Alternative to app_name for launch.

hidden.description: launch only: when true, start the app in the background without bringing it to the foreground.

name: macos_manage_apps

app.description: Frontmost application details. Present for action=frontmost.

window_title.description: Title of the frontmost window, or null if no window is open.

app_name.description: The application acted upon. Present for write actions.

apps.description: Running user-facing applications. Present for action=list.

items.description: Running application with its process details.

bundle_id.description: Bundle identifier, e.g. "com.apple.Safari". Null if unavailable.

frontmost.description: True when this is the frontmost app.

visible.description: True when the app is visible (not hidden).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `app_not_found`: launch names an app_name or bundle_id that matches no installed application. `no_frontmost_app`: frontmost finds no application in front. `not_running`: quit, force_quit, hide, or show called on an app that is not running. `accessibility_required`: An action is denied Accessibility (hide, show) or Automation for the app or System Events it scripts. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

success.description: True when the operation completed successfully. Present for write actions.

title: Manage macOS Apps
